chapter: Piron, Clarence Williams and the ODJB repertoire
title: Piron's 1922 letter about Sister Kate
summary: The interviewer reads A. J. Piron's August 1922 letter to La Rocca thanking him for promoting Sister Kate and offering more numbers.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This is a letter. It says, It says, From A.J. P. Ron, 1734 Annette Street, New Orleans, Louisiana. The dateline is August 13, 1922. Mr. D. James LaRocca, original Dixon and Jazz Band. 421 Sheets Head Bay Road, Brooklyn, New York. My dear Mr. LaRocca, yours of the fifth INST comp was received and very sorry indeed for the delay and great suspense that you no doubt suffered. But only to the fact that I was out of the city, I was unable to answer at once. But I assure you that I have taken great interest in saying, and in the future you can rest assured that all correspondents will receive my prompt attention. I'm not aware of the fact that you all are the starters of Sister Kate up north. That's quote Sister Kate, unquote, up north. But I wish to express my delight in being informed of saying through your letter of the fifth. And assure you that you will receive all assistance that I can give along the lines of placing this and all of the numbers that I have and that you may be able to use. I'm sorry indeed that you were put to such inconvenience in trying to locate me. And again, I am glad that you succeeded. As far as bands are concerned, you can rest assured that I will put forth every effort to keep them supplied with my numbers. And I really haven't the language to express my thanks for the splendid efforts made by both you and your band. Speaking of the victor concern, I feel sure that you will... Better read this slowly. Speaking of the victor concern, I feel sure that you will... I feel assured that you will meet with tremendous success due to the wide reputation of your aggregation. And while I am at it, and aside from Sister Kate, I am sending you to look over. If your man is like my man, that's a quote, if your man is like my man, unquote. And several others that have recently came into the limelight here. And I believe that from your letter of the fifth, we'll go over also for reasons aforementioned. In reference to paragraph five of your letter, we'll say that I am unable to make a complete statement concerning... Turning it over to a large pub concern, that's capital P-U-B concern. I presume that means publishing. Publishing concern. As I have already several contracts from different concerns to be considered. But in the meantime, I will appreciate anything you might do to record Sister Kate or any other number of mine. You can rest assured that you will be greatly recompensated for saying. Now in the event that any concern approach you with their willingness to accept, that's E-X-E-E-P-T, quote, Sister Kate, unquote, or any other number, you will do well to wire or write me at once so you will give me a chance to demonstrate to you my thanks. For some time I have felt that the title, quote, I wish that I could shimmy like my Sister Kate, unquote, was a little out of date. And for that reason I have changed it to, quote, Sister Kate, unquote, with a rearrangement of lyrics, and on a few days you will receive the new outfit, which I hope you can use to great advantage. Now trusting that you will be able to use the numbers that I am sending under separate cover, I am very, yours very truly, AJP Rome, and that has initials J-C-R-A-J-P.
